1. Getting started

rsi is a keyboard-driven TUI over the rsid daemon, which runs and persists every agent session. Start rsi; on Linux and macOS it starts rsid if no daemon is accepting connections and the daemon binary is available. Press ? for help on the focused view, then s for the searchable symbol legend. Inside help, Tab and Shift-Tab cycle contextual keys, all commands and symbols. Press : or <Space>; for the command palette, and <Space> as the leader for most commands. This manual is generated from the running build's registries, so what it lists is what the build does.

Discovery

<Space>BCreate BugCreates a Bug leaf under the current Epic.

:manager restart [arg]Operator quiet-point restartShows the pending quiet-point restart; :manager restart now forces it and :manager restart cancel cancels it.

8. Lifecycle and housekeeping

Launch, continue, interrupt, archive, delete, rotate and retry sessions, stop all spend, and manage panes and tabs.

Session

KeysCommandActionWhat it does
yyCopy Session UUIDCopies the selected session's UUID; in a transcript yy copies the selected event's content instead.
x:kill :kiSoft interrupt running sessionRequests a soft stop (currently SIGINT fallback) and marks the session SOFT; a granted manager may restart it.
XINTERRUPT NOWPress twice within five seconds to cancel the active turn and mark it HARD.
<Space>hs:pause softDowngrade hard pause to softChanges the selected session's HARD marker to SOFT so a granted manager may restart it.
<Space>hc:pause clearClear operator pauseClears the selected session's SOFT or HARD marker; a manager seat shows its age and any held succession, and the key must be pressed twice to confirm.
<Space>hu:provider-clear-holdClear provider usage holdAfter switching accounts, ignores the selected session’s provider’s old plan windows and releases held work. Fresh usage readings still enforce limits.
<Space>c:continue [arg] :cont [arg]Continue selected session<Space>c sends literal continue; :continue opens a prompt, and :continue <text> sends text directly.
PPin or unpin selected sessionPins or unpins the selected session at the top of the list.
<Space>a:archive :arcArchive selected sessionArchives the selected session (reversible with U from the Archive zone).
UUnarchive selected sessionRestores the selected archived session to the Main zone.
<Space>tToggle testing-needed markerMarks or clears the testing-needed flag on the selected leaf session.

:manager-reseat [arg]Reseat failed managerReplaces the selected session's project manager seat, whose provider is down, with a new session on another provider that keeps the seat's scope, policy, lineage and the hub's dispatch reach; :manager-reseat <provider>[/<model>] <reason>. Run twice to confirm.
:cold-restoreRestore from cold storagePuts the focused archived session's rows back from the cold-storage archive into the live database (:cold-restore). A session that is not in cold storage answers that it is already live. Reading a cold session needs no restore: its transcript is whole either way.

9. Diagnostics and tools

Operator views: diagnostics, memory search, graph review, the recursive DAG browser, notifications and questions.

Operator Views

KeysCommandActionWhat it does
<Space>i:issuesOpen or focus Issues workspaceOpens the Issues workspace pane for the current project, or focuses it if already open.
:issue [arg]Open an issue by numberOpens the Issues workspace on the issue with the given number (:issue 2377 or :issue #2377), including closed and archived issues; without a number it opens the go-to-number prompt.
:cold-archive [arg]Cold-storage archive:cold-archive shows the archive's state (live database and archive sizes, sessions staged, verified and cold, the last pass and any problem); :cold-archive run starts a stage pass (copy and verify, delete nothing), move also deletes the verified rows from the live database (only while a fresh rsi.db backup exists) and reclaims their pages, verify re-reads every archived chunk and compact schedules the one-time database compaction for the next supervised restart.
:external-reports [arg]External reports:external-reports shows the external harness-report import (#3789): the last sync, reports seen, imported and linked as duplicates, and any error; :external-reports sync runs one import pass now with the hub's own gh login; :external-reports filter filters the focused Issues pane to the external-report label. 11. Settings reference

Every settings row by group and section: what it does, what kind of value it is, where the value lives, and when a change applies.

Settings

KeysCommandActionWhat it does
Settings: h LeftReturn to categoriesReturns focus from the settings items to the category rail. On a numeric setting row it steps the value down like a slider (l / Right step up); use Tab or Esc to leave such a row.
Settings: l RightEnter selected categoryMoves focus from the category rail into the selected category's items. On a numeric setting row it steps the value up like a slider (h / Left step down), staged until you apply with w.
Settings: SpaceToggle or activate settingToggles a boolean setting, cycles a choice, types a number into a numeric row, or activates the selected settings row.
Settings: aAdd itemAdds an item to the selected settings list (hooks, providers, budgets and similar lists).
Settings: dDelete itemDeletes the selected item from a settings list; in Provider Keys, d arms and a second d confirms clearing the slot.
Settings: eEnable or disable skillEnables or disables the selected Claude skill.
Settings: KMove navigator column earlierMoves the selected optional navigator column one place left; the order is saved per navigator preset.
Settings: JMove navigator column laterMoves the selected optional navigator column one place right; the order is saved per navigator preset.
Settings: +Step setting upMoves the selected setting to its next value (switches on): numeric rows stop at their maximum, choices wrap. The value is staged until you apply with w.
Settings: -Step setting downMoves the selected setting to its previous value (switches off): numeric rows stop at their minimum, choices wrap. The value is staged until you apply with w.
Settings: wApply pending settingsApplies every staged setting at once: ONE atomic daemon update carries every changed field with its final value (all of them take effect or none do), plus the local preferences. Esc or q discards them instead.
Settings: RRefresh daemon-backed stateRe-reads daemon-backed settings state (config, hooks, skills, storage).
Settings: sSet provider keyOpens the masked Set form for the selected provider key slot.
Settings: rRotate provider keyOpens the masked Rotate form for the selected provider key slot.
Settings: cCheck provider keyChecks the selected provider key slot with its provider.
Settings: iImport provider keysImports available provider keys from the process environment into vault slots.
Settings: /Search settingsOpens an incremental settings query; Enter jumps to the first match at or after the cursor.
Settings: nNext settings matchJumps to the next settings row matching the active query, wrapping with a notice.
Settings: NPrevious settings matchJumps to the previous settings row matching the active query, wrapping with a notice.
<Space>,:set :settingsOpen settingsOpens the settings pane.
:hooksOpen hook settingsOpens settings at the Claude hooks list.
:skillsOpen skill settingsOpens settings at the Claude skills list.

Changing an armed cap keeps its baseline; 0 turns it off and forgets the baseline. While armed, OpenRouter-billed launches (the OpenRouter provider on any route, and Harness sessions on the OpenRouter endpoint) are refused with openrouter_spend_cap_reached once spend plus a small per-launch reserve reaches the stop line, and also refused (openrouter_spend_cap_probe_stale) whenever the account usage could not be probed for five minutes; a running Harness session ends at its next model call past the line.actiondaemon field openrouter_spend_cap_usdwhen activated

SettingWhat it doesKindStored inApplies

Coordinator context cap (0 off, 1-100 = % of window)Live context at which a manager seat, area manager, Epic lead or global manager is rotated with a daemon-written handoff. Read or set a provider or model override with :context-cap <Provider[/model]> [pct|tokens|default]. Default 60 (60% of the session's known context window). Values 1-100 are a percentage of the window, 32000-2000000 are tokens, 0 turns it off. An unknown window disables percentage caps. Needs context rotation on.choicedaemon field coordinator_context_cap_tokenswhen applied · no restart
Manager wake-turn cap (per hour, 0 off)Wake-driven turns a manager seat may start per rolling hour before the daemon coalesces its routine notices (a lead's state, work rows, non-blocked intents) into the next free slot (0 off, else 1-60, default 0). A manager cannot refuse a wake, so a turn-rate cap in prose does not hold. With a cap set, a seat that has used it keeps routine-only deliveries armed and reads them in one coalesced turn when a turn ages out of the hour. Mail, operator answers, failures, gates, merge-queue and satellite outcomes and safety anomalies are never held; one delivered past a spent cap is counted as a bypass. The seat's turns used, coalesced wakes and bypasses show in its coordinator budget (authority catalog and the global manager seat views). It applies to the next delivery; a self-armed wake (a job end or timer the seat set) is not held.choicedaemon field manager_max_turns_per_hourwhen applied · no restart
Worker context cap (0 off, 1-100 = % of window)Live context at which a worker with a launching manager or Epic lead is told to pass the baton (commit, append a handoff to its Issue, end its turn) and its launcher gets a worker_context_cap notice. Read or set a provider or model override with :worker-context-cap <Provider[/model]> [pct|tokens|default]. Default 60 (60% of the session's known context window). Values 1-100 are a percentage of the window, 32000-2000000 are tokens, 0 turns it off. Managers may propose it within operator bounds.choicedaemon field worker_context_cap_tokenswhen applied · no restart
Provider lifecycle hooksLifecycle hooks a new Claude or Codex session installs beyond the custody and mail hooks: none (default), or any set of StopFailure, PreCompact and SessionStart. StopFailure (Claude) records an API error that ended a turn as a typed provider-error row; PreCompact (Claude and Codex) records that the provider is about to compact the context, so the baton/handoff logic can act before it does. SessionStart (Claude and Codex) delivers the session's RSI preamble as hook context instead of the start of the first prompt, within the provider's 10,000-character cap per hook. Claude splits long preambles at startup part boundaries into labelled chunks with one handler each; an indivisible part that cannot fit stays in the prompt. Delivery is recorded after every chunk is claimed; a preamble the hook did not deliver goes back in the next turn's prompt. Each hook runs RSI's own rsi-rpc hook command through the same per-session --settings / -c hooks.* path as the custody and mail hooks (Codex trusts it by key and hash, checked by the contract canary). A hook that fails to run is skipped: it never blocks or ends a session. none installs exactly the custody and mail hooks.choicedaemon field provider_lifecycle_hooksnext spawn

Codex live model catalog TTL (s)Seconds the per-login Codex model list is cached before it is read again (0 = bundled catalog only, default 300). The Codex model picker, the manager preflight and launch admission use the models this login can actually use, read from the Codex app-server (model/list) and falling back to non-bundled codex debug models. A failed read falls back to the bundled catalog, marked degraded, and never refuses a launch by itself. A model absent from a fresh live list is refused model_unavailable before any session or sandbox is created, and admitted again as soon as a later list contains it. 0 reads only the bundled catalog.choicedaemon field codex_live_catalog_ttl_secswhen applied · no restart
Codex plan-window poll (s)Seconds between reads of the Codex plan windows (0 = off, default 300). The daemon asks the Codex app-server (account/rateLimits/read, no model turn) how much of the signed-in plan's windows is used and stores them beside Claude's, so launch admission, the manager capacity view and the status bar treat both providers alike. A failed read keeps the last windows and marks them stale; a logged-out login stores nothing. 0 turns the poll off (Claude windows are unaffected).choicedaemon field codex_rate_limit_poll_secswhen applied · no restart
Provider CLI contract canaryChecks, at daemon start and when a CLI's version changes, that the installed Claude Code and Codex still honour what RSI relies on (default on). A bounded, non-billing check per CLI: Codex hook trust and the app-server handshake (hooks/list with RSI's real hook overrides: both session-flag hooks must be trusted with RSI's hash), and Claude's initialize control request plus every flag RSI passes (help text, then an unknown-option probe for hidden flags) and the non-bare ambient login. A failed check marks the provider degraded with a reason code in the provider status and the Provider Keys list, and notifies the manager. Off skips the check and reports the provider unchecked.toggledaemon field provider_contract_canarywhen applied · no restart
Refuse Codex launch when custody hook is untrustedRefuses a Codex launch when the canary finds the installed codex-cli does not trust RSI's sandbox custody hook (default on). The custody hook stops a Codex session from switching the sandbox branch, stashing, or force-pushing. If a codex-cli update changes how it hashes hooks, the hook is silently not run. With this on, a Codex launch that needs the hook is refused with codex_hook_untrusted, codex_hook_hash_mismatch or codex_hook_missing until RSI's hash is updated; off launches Codex without custody and only reports the provider degraded. Only a definite untrusted result refuses: an unchecked or failed canary never does.toggledaemon field codex_refuse_untrusted_custody_hookwhen applied · no restart
Claude project config isolationIsolation of Claude project config for new Claude processes: off, settings or strict.choicedaemon field claude_config_isolationnext spawn
Codex user config isolationIsolation of the operator's Codex config for new Codex processes: off, user (ignore config.toml), rules (ignore execpolicy rules) or all. user passes --ignore-user-config so $CODEX_HOME/config.toml (model, profile, mcp_servers, hooks, approval_policy) is not loaded; rules passes --ignore-rules so user and project execpolicy .rules files are not loaded; all passes both. Auth still uses CODEX_HOME and every override RSI passes still applies. off adds no flag.choicedaemon field codex_config_isolationnext spawn
Provider launch overridesExtra Claude Code / Codex CLI launch options, from an allowlist (default none). Enter opens a JSON editor; the daemon checks each option and the editor shows its reason when it refuses. A JSON object of per-provider lists, e.g. {"codex":["model_reasoning_summary=concise"],"claude":["--append-system-prompt=Be terse."]}. Claude takes the flags --append-system-prompt and --betas (passed as --flag=value; the fallback chain and spend cap have their own settings); Codex takes the config keys model_reasoning_summary, model_verbosity, service_tier, web_search, hide_agent_reasoning, show_raw_agent_reasoning and agents.enabled (passed as -c key=value). Anything that widens privilege (--dangerously-skip-permissions, --permission-mode, --add-dir, permissions.*, sandbox.*, hooks.*, approval_policy, sandbox_mode, mcp_servers.*) or that RSI sets itself (model, effort, resume, --fallback-model, --max-budget-usd, and the Codex subagent model and concurrency cap, which have their own settings) is refused with provider_launch_override_denied; any other key with provider_launch_override_unknown_key, as is a Claude flag the installed CLI does not know. Applied at the next CLI launch (each Claude turn) and recorded on the session as a launch-overrides row. Empty clears.actiondaemon field provider_launch_overrideswhen activated

Enter opens a text editor. Passed as --fallback-model=a,b to each new Claude CLI session (#2762); the CLI tries them in order per turn and retries the primary at the start of each turn. It does not apply to auth, billing or rate-limit errors, and is not passed to Bedrock-routed models or when the list names only the session's own model. A result that shows a chain member served part of the run adds a model_fallback_used row (from, to) to the session transcript. A background pass runs at most every 6 hours at the lowest CPU and I/O priority, outside startup. It writes each cold session's tool rows to an append-only archive file under the archive directory, fsyncs it and reads it back against its checksums; only then, and only while a backup of rsi.db younger than 24 hours exists in ~/.rsi/backups (the pass takes one itself when none does), it deletes those rows from the live database and returns the freed space in small steps. Transcripts still open whole; :cold-restore puts a session's rows back. Shrinking the file once happens at the next supervised restart (:cold-archive compact asks for it). A weekly pass re-reads every archived chunk, and every failure raises an operator to-do. The archive directory is the row below; back it up with the rest of ~/.rsi. Read at the start of each pass.choicedaemon field cold_archive_after_dayswhen applied · no restart

The daemon checks the path before saving it and again when a pass starts: a symlink or .. that leads into a sandbox root or a .git directory is refused, and the editor shows the reason and keeps your text. Existing archive files keep their recorded path, so a change only affects new files. Back the directory up with the rest of ~/.rsi.actiondaemon field cold_archive_dirwhen activated
Cold-storage statusLive database size, archive files and sizes, sessions staged, verified and cold, and whether a pass is running; R refreshes it. Read from GetColdArchiveStatus when you open this tab and on R. Open problems (a failed pass, an archive file that failed verification) are listed in the last-run row and by :cold-archive status.read-onlydaemon (cold archive)when applied · no restart
Cold-storage last runThe newest archive pass: its mode, outcome, how many sessions it staged and moved, the bytes written and any problem; R refreshes it.read-onlydaemon (cold archive)when applied · no restart
Run cold-storage passStarts a copy-only archive pass now (stage and verify) in the background; the archive must be switched on. :cold-archive move also moves the rows out, :cold-archive verify re-reads every archived chunk.actiondaemon (cold archive)when activated

:cold-archive [arg]Cold-storage archive:cold-archive shows the archive's state (live database and archive sizes, sessions staged, verified and cold, the last pass and any problem); :cold-archive run starts a stage pass (copy and verify, delete nothing), move also deletes the verified rows from the live database (only while a fresh rsi.db backup exists) and reclaims their pages, verify re-reads every archived chunk and compact schedules the one-time database compaction for the next supervised restart.
:external-reports [arg]External reports:external-reports shows the external harness-report import (#3789): the last sync, reports seen, imported and linked as duplicates, and any error; :external-reports sync runs one import pass now with the hub's own gh login; :external-reports filter filters the focused Issues pane to the external-report label. Imported reports are untrusted P4 Issues until triage promotes them.

(adds or removes launches on the node's current grant), configure <JSON> and revoke <node> inspect or change one.

Settings pane

Keys of the settings pane (category rail and items).

KeysActionWhat it does
Ctrl-Alt-GContextual helpOpens contextual help listing the keys and commands available in the current view; Ctrl-Alt-G works even while typing.
?Contextual helpOpens contextual help listing the keys and commands available in the current view; Ctrl-Alt-G works even while typing.
jMove selection or scroll downMoves the selection down one row, or scrolls the focused view down.
kMove selection or scroll upMoves the selection up one row, or scrolls the focused view up.
EnterOpen or activate selectionOpens the selected row: drills into a Group or Epic in place (from session detail it folds open or shut in the sidebar tree), opens a leaf session's detail, or activates the selected setting.
DeleteReset selected roleResets the selected theme role to the active theme's default color.
hReturn to categoriesReturns focus from the settings items to the category rail. On a numeric setting row it steps the value down like a slider (l / Right step up); use Tab or Esc to leave such a row.
LeftReturn to categoriesReturns focus from the settings items to the category rail. On a numeric setting row it steps the value down like a slider (l / Right step up); use Tab or Esc to leave such a row.
lEnter selected categoryMoves focus from the category rail into the selected category's items. On a numeric setting row it steps the value up like a slider (h / Left step down), staged until you apply with w.
RightEnter selected categoryMoves focus from the category rail into the selected category's items. On a numeric setting row it steps the value up like a slider (h / Left step down), staged until you apply with w.
SpaceToggle or activate settingToggles a boolean setting, cycles a choice, types a number into a numeric row, or activates the selected settings row.
aAdd itemAdds an item to the selected settings list (hooks, providers, budgets and similar lists).
dDelete itemDeletes the selected item from a settings list; in Provider Keys, d arms and a second d confirms clearing the slot.
eEnable or disable skillEnables or disables the selected Claude skill.
KMove navigator column earlierMoves the selected optional navigator column one place left; the order is saved per navigator preset.
JMove navigator column laterMoves the selected optional navigator column one place right; the order is saved per navigator preset.
+Step setting upMoves the selected setting to its next value (switches on): numeric rows stop at their maximum, choices wrap. The value is staged until you apply with w.
-Step setting downMoves the selected setting to its previous value (switches off): numeric rows stop at their minimum, choices wrap. The value is staged until you apply with w.
wApply pending settingsApplies every staged setting at once: ONE atomic daemon update carries every changed field with its final value (all of them take effect or none do), plus the local preferences. Esc or q discards them instead.
RRefresh daemon-backed stateRe-reads daemon-backed settings state (config, hooks, skills, storage).
sSet provider keyOpens the masked Set form for the selected provider key slot.
rRotate provider keyOpens the masked Rotate form for the selected provider key slot.
cCheck provider keyChecks the selected provider key slot with its provider.
iImport provider keysImports available provider keys from the process environment into vault slots.
/Search settingsOpens an incremental settings query; Enter jumps to the first match at or after the cursor.
nNext settings matchJumps to the next settings row matching the active query, wrapping with a notice.
NPrevious settings matchJumps to the previous settings row matching the active query, wrapping with a notice.
qClose or cancelCloses the current view or cancels the pending action.
EscClose or cancelCloses the current view or cancels the pending action.

File viewer commands

The file viewer's own : command line (:q closes the viewer, not rsi).

CommandWhat it does
:wSave the file.
:w!Save, overwriting changes made on disk since the file was opened.
:wqSave and close the viewer.
:xSave and close the viewer (same as :wq).
:qClose the viewer; refused while there are unsaved changes.
:q!Close the viewer, discarding unsaved changes.
:quit!Close the viewer, discarding unsaved changes.
:e!Revert the buffer to the version on disk.
:42Jump to a line number (1-based): :<n>.
:set autopairTurn bracket and quote auto-pairing on.
:set noautopairTurn bracket and quote auto-pairing off.
